title.narrative: Emergency WASH and health response for flood affected population of Freetown (Western Area) Sierra L

description.narrative:
This is part of START Fund project.
Heavy rains in Freetown on the 14th August 2017 have caused a mud/landslide in Regent, Western Rural district and, a suburb of Freetown. The number of fatalities is still unknown, but according to the Red Cross (14/08/2017) over 312 bodies have been brought to the city mortuary. The government of Sierra Leone is currently undertaking a search and rescue operation, and expects the number of casualties to increase significantly.
1) House cleaning: While the exact number of houses that are affected, but not structurally damaged, is not yet known, this response will target 500 homes, i.e. benefitting an estimated 2,500 people, for cleaning and minor repairs to restore them to a state that is fit for safe and dignified habitation. This activity will target homes in the flood affected areas, due to the near complete destruction of homes in the landslide affected areas. This activity fills a gap, as shelter actors are targeting the official temporary shelters. The response will target the most vulnerable among those affected without any discrimination according to ethnicity, religion, gender, socio-economic status, or any other factors.
